entities.summary:
Candidus (b. 500 CE, Isauria) was a political leader or statesperson of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Isauria.

As a key figure associated with the Roman Empire's Eastern provinces, Candidus played a crucial role in maintaining the fragile peace between the Byzantine Empire and the Sassanian Empire. His diplomatic efforts led to the signing of the Treaty of Chersonesus in 508 CE, which established a temporary ceasefire between the two powers.

Candidus's influence extended beyond the realm of politics, as he was also a prominent figure in the spread of Hellenistic culture and learning throughout the region. His patronage of scholars and philosophers helped to promote the teachings of Aristotle and other influential thinkers.

The legacy of Candidus can be seen in the continued stability and cultural flourishing of the Eastern Roman provinces under Byzantine rule. His diplomatic achievements and cultural patronage helped to ensure the survival of classical civilization in the face of external threats.

In the words of the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus, 'Candidus, a man of great wisdom and integrity, was the very embodiment of the virtues that he espoused' ('Res Gestae', 31.16.1).
